name: Bus, coach and school-transport operators

problems.words: Parents call every morning asking where the van is
quick_ideas: Ask drivers to tell the office when they leave the depot, so you know first
Let parents on a late route know as soon as you know, so they hear it from you.

workzap_build.text: a route board with departure and arrival status, and WhatsApp alerts per route sent to parents who have agreed, without storing any child's details.

problems.ask_first: How do you find out today where a van is?
problems.free_stops: How alerts are set up per route is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, count morning calls by route and note the delay reason beside each, so the noisiest route gets attention first.
Give one staff member the job of updating route delays at one fixed morning time, so calls drop because updates leave from the office sooner.

problems.words: Monthly fees from parents come late, some never
quick_ideas: List who has paid this month by route, so you know the gap
Remind late payers once on a fixed date, so it's consistent.

workzap_build.text: a fee and contract tracker sending reminders and receipts straight to clients.

problems.ask_first: Is it the same few families paying late each month, or different ones every time?
problems.free_stops: Reminder steps are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: This week, count unpaid families by route and note how late each account is, so the worst collection route stops being guessed.
Give one person one route wise dues list and a fixed reminder day each month, so follow up happens consistently before balances age further.

problems.words: Schools or companies pay our invoices after months
quick_ideas: List each client's open invoices by age, so you know who to chase first
Agree one payments contact at each client, so chasing goes to the right person.

workzap_build.text: contract invoices with ageing and monthly trip reports generated for each client.

problems.ask_first: Which pay slower, the schools or the companies?
problems.free_stops: Statement and report layouts are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: This week, note each school or company invoice date beside its payment date, so the slowest paying clients are clear in one glance.
Give one staff member one notebook for all client invoices and follow ups, so unpaid bills stop getting missed between calls and visits.

problems.words: Drivers don't show up and we scramble for a replacement
quick_ideas: Ask drivers to confirm the evening before, so gaps are found early
Keep a short list of standby drivers, so one absence doesn't stop a route.

workzap_build.text: a driver roster and attendance with quick replacement and duty-hour logs.

problems.ask_first: Does this come up mostly on Mondays and after holidays, or at random through the week?
problems.free_stops: Roster rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, note which routes needed replacement drivers and when the absence was known, so the worst scramble points show.
Give one dispatcher the evening confirmation list in one notebook, so replacement calls start earlier when a driver is missing.

problems.words: Fuel cost per bus is going up and I can't tell why
quick_ideas: Record each fill with kilometres per vehicle, so fuel can be set against distance
Compare vehicles on similar routes, so outliers stand out.

workzap_build.text: a fuel log per vehicle and route with comparisons and flags on unusual use.

problems.ask_first: Is the rise across all buses, or mainly a few older ones on certain routes?
problems.free_stops: How comparisons are made is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: This week, compare fuel bought against each bus's route distance and note the biggest mismatch, so one bus or route can be checked closely.
Give one person one page per bus for fuel slips and distance notes, so rising fuel use gets spotted before month end.

problems.words: Conductors collect fares and some cash doesn't reach the office
quick_ideas: Issue numbered tickets on every trip, so fares can be counted
Count each conductor's cash against tickets at trip end, so gaps show the same day.

workzap_build.text: conductor cash matched against tickets per trip.

problems.ask_first: Is the missing cash mostly on a few routes, or across most conductors?
problems.free_stops: The cash-up steps are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, compare each trip's cash handed in with passenger counts from the same trip, so the leakage point narrows fast.
Give one office person the end of trip cash check in one place, so conductors hand over against the same record every day.

problems.words: Breakdowns on route with no backup plan
quick_ideas: List each vehicle's kilometres and last service, so due ones are visible
Decide which vehicle covers which route if one breaks down, so there's a plan.

workzap_build.text: a maintenance schedule with a breakdown log and backup vehicle assignment.

problems.ask_first: Do breakdowns come mostly from a few old vehicles, or across the whole fleet?
problems.free_stops: Service intervals and backup rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: This week, note every route delay caused by a vehicle problem and which bus it involved, so the most disruptive bus becomes visible.
Give one supervisor one written fallback bus list for each route, so dispatch can switch vehicles quickly when a bus fails.

problems.words: Seat bookings from counter, phone and online aren't combined
quick_ideas: Keep one seat list per departure that every channel checks, so seats aren't sold twice
Note no-shows per trip, so you see the pattern.

workzap_build.text: one seat booking list combining counter and online sales, with seat locks and no-show tracking.

problems.ask_first: Which channel causes most of the double selling, the counter, the phone or online?
problems.free_stops: How channels connect is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, count how many seats were promised twice or left empty on each departure, so the biggest booking clash is measured.
Give one person one master departure list kept at the counter, so phone and walk in bookings check the same seat picture.

problems.words: Permit, fitness and insurance renewals are always last minute
quick_ideas: List every vehicle's renewal dates in one place, so nothing comes as a surprise
Look ahead a month every week, so there's time to act.

workzap_build.text: a renewal tracker for permits, fitness and insurance with reminders.

problems.ask_first: Is it mostly one kind of renewal, such as permit, fitness or insurance, that gets left late?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timings are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: This week, count renewals due soon by vehicle and note which papers caused last minute chasing before, so the admin load is visible early.
Give one staff member one renewal diary checked on the same day each week, so paperwork stops surfacing only at the last minute.

problems.words: I don't know which route actually makes money
quick_ideas: Pick a few routes and list what each earned and cost last month, so you get a first picture
Go over it with your accountant, so the figures are read correctly.

workzap_build.text: route profitability with revenue against fuel, driver cost and dead mileage.

problems.ask_first: Do you have a rough feel for which few routes are strongest, or no idea at all?
problems.free_stops: Which costs are included is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one week, note each route's passengers, fuel slips and driver hours together, so weaker routes stop hiding inside busy ones.
Give one office person a single notebook for every route's daily takings and running costs, so route profit gets reviewed from one place.

never_say: Advice on licensing, route permits, fitness standards, driver hours or child-safety rules.
Anything that asks for or stores children's names, photos, addresses or stops tied to a child.
Help falsifying fitness certificates, overloading or forging attendance or trip records.
Covert monitoring of staff or passengers.
Comment on fare or fee levels.
For an accident, a child left on a bus or a medical emergency, anything before pointing to emergency services.

sample_reply.person: I run school vans in Lahore and my phone doesn't stop every morning, parents asking where the van is. What can be done?
sample_reply.pi:
Sure, this can be sorted, and the first steps are simple.
First, ask drivers to tell the office when they leave the depot, so you know before parents ask.
Second, let parents on a late route know as soon as you know, so they hear it from you.
For a lasting fix, Workzap could set up: a route board with live departure and arrival status and WhatsApp alerts to parents, without storing any child's details.
